title: Participles and Compound Tenses
summary: Use regular and irregular participles in compound tenses, passive forms, and adjective-like uses.

sections.heading: Regular participles
sections.body: Regular past participles end in **-ado** for -ar verbs and **-ido** for -er/-ir verbs. With **ter**, they form compound tenses and usually do not agree.

examples.en: I have been studying a lot.
We have been dividing the tasks.

sections.heading: Common irregular participles
sections.body: Many frequent verbs have irregular participles: **abrir → aberto**, **dizer → dito**, **fazer → feito**, **escrever → escrito**, **ver → visto**, **pôr → posto**.

examples.pt: Você já tinha visto esse filme?
examples.en: Had you already seen this movie?

sections.heading: Participles as adjectives
sections.body: When participles function like adjectives or appear in passive voice with **ser/estar**, they agree with the noun in gender and number.

keyPoints: With ter, participles are normally invariable: tenho feito.
With ser/estar as passive or adjective, participles agree.
Many high-frequency verbs have irregular participles.

commonMistakes.note: With ter, the participle does not agree.
